# Jubilees Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Three Visitors; Sodom Destroyed; Isaac's Birth; Feast of Tabernacles

---

**16:1** And on the new moon of the fourth month we appeared unto Abraham at the oak of Mamre, and we talked with him, and we announced to him that a son would be given to him by Sarah his wife.

**16:2** And Sarah laughed, for she heard that we had spoken these words with Abraham, and we rebuked her.

**16:3** And she was afraid and denied it, saying: "I laughed not"; for she was afraid of us.

**16:4** And we told her the name of her son, as his name is ordained and written in the heavenly tablets, namely Isaac.

**16:5** And when we departed from Abraham, we turned to Sodom; and Abraham came with us to bring us on the way.

**16:6** And the LORD said: "Shall I hide from Abraham what I do, seeing that I know he will command his children and his household after him, that they keep the way of the LORD to do justice and judgment; that the LORD may bring upon Abraham all that he has spoken of him?"

**16:7** And we will destroy this place for the wickedness of its inhabitants before the LORD.

**16:8** And Abraham drew near and said: "Will thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked? And what if there be fifty righteous within the city? Wilt thou not spare it for the sake of fifty righteous that are therein?"

**16:9** "Far be it from thee to do such a thing, to slay the righteous with the wicked, and that the righteous should be as the wicked. Far be it from thee. Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?"

**16:10** And the LORD said: "If I find fifty righteous within the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake."

**16:11** And Abraham answered: "Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the LORD, who am but dust and ashes."

**16:12** And he bargained with the LORD from fifty down to ten, and the LORD said: "I will not destroy it for ten's sake."

**16:13** And we came to Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gate of Sodom, and when he saw us, he rose to meet us, and he bowed himself with his face toward the ground.

**16:14** And he said: "Now, my lords, turn in to your servant's house, and tarry all night, and wash your feet, and ye shall rise up early, and go on your ways."

**16:15** And they said: "Nay; but we will abide in the street all night." And he pressed upon them greatly, and they turned in unto him, and entered into his house.

**16:16** And he made them a feast, and did bake unleavened bread, and they did eat.

**16:17** And before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round about, both old and young, all the people from every quarter.

**16:18** And they called unto Lot, saying: "Where are the men which came in to thee this night? Bring them out unto us, that we may know them."

**16:19** And Lot went out unto them to the door, and shut the door behind him, and said: "I pray you, my brethren, do not so wickedly."

**16:20** "Behold now, I have two daughters which have not known man; let me, I pray you, bring them out unto you, and do ye to them as seemeth good unto you; only unto these men do nothing, for they came under the shadow of my roof."

**16:21** And they said: "Stand back." And they said: "This one fellow came in to sojourn, and he will needs be a judge: now will we deal worse with thee than with them." And they pressed sore upon the man Lot, and came near to break the door.

**16:22** And the men reached forth their hand and pulled Lot into the house and shut the door of the house. And they smote the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

**16:23** And the angels said to Lot: "Hast thou here any besides? Son in law, and thy sons, and thy daughters, and whatsoever thou hast in the city, bring them out of this place."

**16:24** "For we will destroy this place, because the cry of them is waxen great before the face of the LORD; and the LORD hath sent us to destroy it."

**16:25** And Lot went out, and spake unto his sons in law, which married his daughters, and said: "Up, get you out of this place; for the LORD will destroy this city." But he seemed as one that mocked unto his sons in law.

**16:26** And when the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying: "Arise, take thy wife, and thy two daughters, which are here; lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city."

**16:27** And whilst he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the LORD being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.

**16:28** And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said: "Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed."

**16:29** Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven.

**16:30** And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.

**16:31** And in this jubilee Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all who were born of them were given the feast of Tabernacles as an everlasting ordinance.

---
*EMET notes: The angelic narrator speaks in first person ("we appeared unto Abraham," v.1) throughout — the entire Sodom episode is narrated through the angel's eyes. The telling of the heavenly tablets inscription of Isaac's name (v.4) establishes pre-ordination. V.31: the Feast of Tabernacles is ordained within the Abraham narrative — Jubilees' strategy of projecting the entire Mosaic festival calendar back to the patriarchal age.*
